blocks.text: How do we measure the performance of a computer system? Is a higher clock rate always better?

blocks.markdown: In this lesson, we will explore how to measure the performance of a CPU using the CPU performance equation. We will learn about CPU time, clock rate, and cycles per instruction (CPI), and understand why clock rate alone is not a sufficient measure of performance.

blocks.title: CPU Time
blocks.text: CPU time is the actual time the CPU spends computing for a specific task. It is calculated as the product of the number of instructions, the cycles per instruction (CPI), and the clock cycle time.

blocks.markdown: The clock cycle time is the inverse of the clock rate. Therefore, the CPU time can also be expressed in terms of clock rate:

blocks.caption: CPU Time in terms of Clock Rate

blocks.title: Calculating CPU Time
blocks.prompt: A processor executes 1 million instructions with an average CPI of 2.5 and a clock rate of 2 GHz. Calculate the CPU time.

steps.text: First, convert the clock rate to clock cycle time: \( \text{Clock Cycle Time} = \frac{1}{\text{Clock Rate}} = \frac{1}{2 \times 10^9} \) seconds.
Calculate the CPU time using the formula: \( \text{CPU Time} = \text{Instruction Count} \times \text{CPI} \times \text{Clock Cycle Time} \).

blocks.markdown: While clock rate is an important factor, it does not alone determine performance. The CPI and the instruction count also play crucial roles.

blocks.title: Clock Rate Limitations
blocks.text: A higher clock rate does not always mean better performance. Other factors like CPI and instruction count must be considered.

blocks.title: Comparing Two Designs
blocks.prompt: Design A has a clock rate of 3 GHz and a CPI of 1.5. Design B has a clock rate of 2 GHz and a CPI of 1. Calculate the CPU time for both designs assuming they execute 500 million instructions.

steps.text: Calculate the CPU time for Design A: \( \text{CPU Time}_A = \frac{500 \times 10^6 \times 1.5}{3 \times 10^9} \).
Calculate the CPU time for Design B: \( \text{CPU Time}_B = \frac{500 \times 10^6 \times 1}{2 \times 10^9} \).
Both designs have the same CPU time of 0.25 seconds, despite different clock rates and CPIs.

blocks.answer: Both designs have a CPU time of 0.25 seconds.

points: CPU time depends on instruction count, CPI, and clock rate.
Clock rate alone is not a sufficient measure of performance.
The CPU performance equation helps compare different designs.
